stories.title: Farmers call for minister's resignation over cattle cull
stories.summary: The Ulster Farmer's Union says confidence in Andrew Muir and his department is "severely damaged".
stories.post: 📰 NEWS: Farmers call for minister's resignation over cattle cull. The Ulster Farmer's Union says confidence in Andrew Muir and his department is "severely damaged". Source: BBC Science.
article_sentences: A farming union has called for the Agriculture Minister Andrew Muir to resign over his department's investigation into a cull of 51 cattle.
They were shot in County Tyrone in June, leading to complaints about the manner of the cull which was carried out within earshot of members of the public.

The Ulster Farmers' Union (UFU) President John McLenaghan said there were serious concerns about the independence of the Department of Agriculture, Environment and Rural Affairs (Deara) review into the incident.
The union has also called for the immediate resignations of the department's permanent secretary Katrina Godfrey and the Chief Veterinary Officer Brian Dooher.
A review of the cattle cull was announced by Deara earlier this month, but the UFU's Executive Committee met on Thursday night.

In a statement on Friday the UFU said it: "Does not have the confidence in the independence of the review as presently constituted, including the scope of the Terms of Reference and appointment of a single person to conduct it.

"The UFU has consistently maintained that an investigation into an incident of this seriousness must be demonstrably independent, robust and capable of commanding the confidence of farm families and the wider public."
UFU President John McLenaghan said calling for resignations was "not a decision the UFU has taken lightly".
"However, confidence has been severely damaged and the most recent event is just one of many instances where farmers feel that the Department has lost touch with farmers.
"We no longer have confidence that the Department can deliver."
BBC News NI has contacted Deara for a response.
